headline: A Chinese publisher is recalling a novel after what looks like an AI chatbot prompt was printed in the middle of its text.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a small but vivid case of AI slipping into publishing, resting on one report relayed from a Chinese outlet.
importance_line: What changed: a printed novel shipped with an apparent AI prompt left in its text, so buyers are reportedly being offered refunds and the wider question is how AI tools slip into publishing, though the account rests on the publisher's own explanation.
summary: China's Dashang Newspaper reports, as relayed by The Asia Business Daily, that a reader found a sentence that appears to be an AI chatbot prompt printed between paragraphs of a novel's print edition from a Jiangsu publisher. The publisher says it mistakenly treated a prompt from proofreading software as part of the text, says the author is not at fault, and will recall the shipped copies before revising and republishing the book.
notes: Read at The Asia Business Daily (url), which cites Dashang Newspaper as the first reporter; the Chinese original was not opened.
